disease_label_per_paper: Behcet disease with multiple pulmonary artery aneurysms
presentation_summary: Twenty days of cough and intermittent fever followed by recurrent small-volume fresh hemoptysis.
More than 10 kg weight loss over one month, epigastric pain, and vomiting after coughing.
History included recurrent painful oral aphthous ulcers since adolescence and prior right knee effusion.
Labs showed hemoglobin 10.6 g/dL, CRP 63 mg/L, and ESR 53 mm/h.
CT pulmonary angiography showed multiple pulmonary artery aneurysms, largest 52 x 51 x 31 mm with mural thrombus.

observations.source_text_value: recurrent painful oral aphthous ulcers since adolescence
prior episode of right knee effusion requiring aspiration one year earlier
frequent episodes of hemoptysis consisting of small volumes of fresh blood
20-day history of cough and intermittent fever
weight loss exceeding 10 kg over one month
computed tomography pulmonary angiography revealed multiple pulmonary artery aneurysms
largest measuring 52 x 51 x 31 mm in the right lower-lobe pulmonary artery
large partially thrombosed aneurysm with a 12-mm eccentric mural thrombus
observations.quality_note: observed mural thrombosis encoded as high thrombotic event hazard state

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: multiple pulmonary artery aneurysms plus recurrent oral aphthous ulcers and inflammatory features

quality_warnings: Vital signs were described as within normal limits without numeric values.
The pulmonary artery aneurysm itself is structured as ordinary imaging evidence; organism tests were not used as diagnostic evidence.
